claims.assertion: The trip drove 19.2 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, +3.8 km (+24%), so the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty was not met.

GPS isolates one off-route segment 17:37–17:50 that drove 5.85 km where the optimal route covers 2.68 km, adding 3.17 km and straying up to 1172 m from the optimal route — an unexempted detour segment.

The rider only asked to 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a location, and the driver's own statement says he picked 'the one I know'; the stop was in fact 5306 m from the pickup and 4755 m from the drop-off, i.e. a driver-chosen far-off detour never told to the rider in advance, so the stop request does not exempt that segment.

No traffic justification exists: traffic records show no incidents near the route during the trip window, only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is not band 1 or 2 congestion and in any case cannot exempt a segment on its own.

The rider's consent was given at 17:33 before the detour start at 17:37, but it covered only 'a stop on the way' with no named place, so it does not cover the driver's chosen 1172 m-off-route diversion to a specific store.

This is RydeTAXI metered service, so the detour's extra kilometres enter the metered fare and are refundable: the bill shows distance $27.11 over 19.2 km, i.e. $1.41/km, and the excess distance was billed $5.30 (3.8 km × $1.41/km).

Applying the RD-2 formula to the unexempted segment's added distance (3.17 km × $1.41/km) yields a partial refund of $4.47, plus the ERP/toll component of that segment if any was charged under FARE-1.
The stop itself lasted 4 min 10 s and produced a $1.08 waiting charge: RydeTAXI waiting time is billed per meter unit and is not refundable under the policy, so we do not contest it.
The driver's account shows 4 disputes and 2 upheld in 90 days, which supports sending his account for review once this detour is upheld; the profile is relied on only as an additional action.

weaknesses: Consent was given before the detour began (F9, F10 at 17:33 vs segment start 17:37), so the driver will argue RD-5 exempts the whole detour; our answer is that the consent named no location while the chosen store was 5306 m from the pickup (F2), so it cannot have covered that specific route change.

The rider was billed no item that is facially unpublishable: distance and time are metered fare components (F8), and the $1.08 waiting charge matches the 4 min 10 s stop (F2, F6), so the driver will argue the bill is legitimate meter output.

The rider's own profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16), which the driver may use to paint the complaint as unmerited; the driver's countervailing record (F17) is only an additional-action basis, never proof of this detour.

claims.assertion: The rider asked in-app at 17:33 for a stop 'at a 7-Eleven on the way' and the driver accepted ('Ok'), so a passenger-requested stop exists in the chat record.

The rider named no specific 7-Eleven; the driver chose the store himself and the GPS track shows that choice generated the off-route segment 17:37–17:50, which added 3.17 km and reached 1172 m from the optimal route, so that segment is not excused by the stop request.

The driver did not tell the rider the chosen location before leaving the optimal route (no chat message between 17:33 and the 17:37 segment start), so the consent condition of RD-5 is not met for that segment.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is neither incident evidence nor a band 1–2 record capable of excusing a reroute.

The off-route driving of 3.17 km (F4), not the gross 3.8 km excess (F1), is the maximum distance-based overcharge on this metered RydeTAXI trip; at the fare's own per-km rate of $1.41 (F5, F8) this is $4.47.

The stationary time of 4 min 10 s (F2) is a mid-trip stop, which RD-3(c) permits RydeTAXI to charge as metered waiting time; the $1.08 waiting charge (F6, 4.2 min × $0.26/min) is therefore properly billed and should not be refunded.

The $5.30 'excess distance billed' line (F5) is not a separate add-on: it is the distance component already inside the $27.11 distance charge and the $41.17 metered total (F8), so refunding it in addition to the RD-2 mileage refund would double-count.

The driver's good record (4.2 years, 4.83 rating, 386 trips in 90 days) and the profile's zero upheld route-deviation disputes count against escalation, and RD-6's flag_account is not triggered because the route-dispute upheld count is 0, not ≥ 1.

weaknesses: F4 and F1 are system records that contradict the driver's statement (F11) that the detour was simply the requested 7-Eleven: an unannounced 5.85 km detour reaching 1172 m off the optimal route for a '2-minute' stop (F9) will be read as a route deviation.

RD-3(b)/RD-5 are squarely against the driver: the rider named no location (F9) and the driver never messaged the location before leaving the optimal route (F10, F4), so the segment's 3.17 km is not excused by the stop request.
No traffic excuse is available (F14 no incidents; F12/F13 are only band 4, which under RD-4(b) is not even sufficient on its own), so the whole 3.17 km stands exposed.
The driver's own profile (F17) shows 4 disputes in 90 days with 2 upheld, which the rider will use to argue a pattern even though neither upheld dispute was a route case.

claims.assertion: The trip drove 19.2 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, +3.8 km (+24%), so the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty was not met.

GPS isolates one off-route segment 17:37–17:50 that drove 5.85 km where the optimal route covers 2.68 km, adding 3.17 km and straying up to 1172 m from the optimal route — an unexempted detour segment.

The rider only asked to 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a location, and the driver's own statement says he picked 'the one I know'; the stop was in fact 5306 m from the pickup and 4755 m from the drop-off, i.e. a driver-chosen far-off detour never told to the rider in advance, so the stop request does not exempt that segment.

No traffic justification exists: traffic records show no incidents near the route during the trip window, only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is not band 1 or 2 congestion and in any case cannot exempt a segment on its own.

The rider's consent was given at 17:33 before the detour start at 17:37, but it covered only 'a stop on the way' with no named place, so it does not cover the driver's chosen 1172 m-off-route diversion to a specific store.

This is RydeTAXI metered service, so the detour's extra kilometres enter the metered fare and are refundable: the bill shows distance $27.11 over 19.2 km, i.e. $1.41/km, and the excess distance was billed $5.30 (3.8 km × $1.41/km).

Applying the RD-2 formula to the unexempted segment's added distance (3.17 km × $1.41/km) yields a partial refund of $4.47, plus the ERP/toll component of that segment if any was charged under FARE-1.
The stop itself lasted 4 min 10 s and produced a $1.08 waiting charge: RydeTAXI waiting time is billed per meter unit and is not refundable under the policy, so we do not contest it.
The driver's account shows 4 disputes and 2 upheld in 90 days, which supports sending his account for review once this detour is upheld; the profile is relied on only as an additional action.

weaknesses: Consent was given before the detour began (F9, F10 at 17:33 vs segment start 17:37), so the driver will argue RD-5 exempts the whole detour; our answer is that the consent named no location while the chosen store was 5306 m from the pickup (F2), so it cannot have covered that specific route change.

The rider was billed no item that is facially unpublishable: distance and time are metered fare components (F8), and the $1.08 waiting charge matches the 4 min 10 s stop (F2, F6), so the driver will argue the bill is legitimate meter output.

The rider's own profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16), which the driver may use to paint the complaint as unmerited; the driver's countervailing record (F17) is only an additional-action basis, never proof of this detour.

claims.assertion: The rider asked in-app at 17:33 for a stop 'at a 7-Eleven on the way' and the driver accepted ('Ok'), so a passenger-requested stop exists in the chat record.

The rider named no specific 7-Eleven; the driver chose the store himself and the GPS track shows that choice generated the off-route segment 17:37–17:50, which added 3.17 km and reached 1172 m from the optimal route, so that segment is not excused by the stop request.

The driver did not tell the rider the chosen location before leaving the optimal route (no chat message between 17:33 and the 17:37 segment start), so the consent condition of RD-5 is not met for that segment.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is neither incident evidence nor a band 1–2 record capable of excusing a reroute.

The off-route driving of 3.17 km (F4), not the gross 3.8 km excess (F1), is the maximum distance-based overcharge on this metered RydeTAXI trip; at the fare's own per-km rate of $1.41 (F5, F8) this is $4.47.

The stationary time of 4 min 10 s (F2) is a mid-trip stop, which RD-3(c) permits RydeTAXI to charge as metered waiting time; the $1.08 waiting charge (F6, 4.2 min × $0.26/min) is therefore properly billed and should not be refunded.

The $5.30 'excess distance billed' line (F5) is not a separate add-on: it is the distance component already inside the $27.11 distance charge and the $41.17 metered total (F8), so refunding it in addition to the RD-2 mileage refund would double-count.

The driver's good record (4.2 years, 4.83 rating, 386 trips in 90 days) and the profile's zero upheld route-deviation disputes count against escalation, and RD-6's flag_account is not triggered because the route-dispute upheld count is 0, not ≥ 1.

weaknesses: F4 and F1 are system records that contradict the driver's statement (F11) that the detour was simply the requested 7-Eleven: an unannounced 5.85 km detour reaching 1172 m off the optimal route for a '2-minute' stop (F9) will be read as a route deviation.

RD-3(b)/RD-5 are squarely against the driver: the rider named no location (F9) and the driver never messaged the location before leaving the optimal route (F10, F4), so the segment's 3.17 km is not excused by the stop request.
No traffic excuse is available (F14 no incidents; F12/F13 are only band 4, which under RD-4(b) is not even sufficient on its own), so the whole 3.17 km stands exposed.
The driver's own profile (F17) shows 4 disputes in 90 days with 2 upheld, which the rider will use to argue a pattern even though neither upheld dispute was a route case.

Agreed, and this is the driver's own concession that the 3.17 km off-route segment is unexempted under RD-3(b); our case rests on exactly that segment (F4), so no mileage beyond it is claimed.
Conceded: no message between 17:33 and the 17:37 segment start names the chosen store (F9, F10, F4), so RD-5 gives the driver no consent defence for that segment.
Conceded: F14 records no incident and F12/F13 are only band 4, so RD-4 provides no exemption and the full 3.17 km stands.

We accept the driver's own arithmetic: 3.17 km × the fare's own $1.41/km rate (F4, F5, F8) = $4.47, which is precisely our revised ask under RD-2; the gross 3.8 km (F1) includes map-matching residue we do not claim.
Conceded: the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) was a passenger-requested mid-trip halt and RD-3(c) lets RydeTAXI charge metered waiting time (F6), so we withdraw any challenge to the $1.08 waiting charge.

Agreed that the $5.30 line is not a separate add-on (F5, F8); we never asked for it on top of the mileage refund — our claim is only the RD-2 formula applied to the unexempted segment's added km (F4).

The driver's clean route history and length of service (F17) are noted, but RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and F17 shows 0 for route disputes, so we drop the flag_account request and ask only for the RD-2 refund.

We accept the raw distances (F1) but note the +3.8 km is the net figure; the only policy-recognised deviation is the single off-route segment adding 3.17 km (F4), and RD-1/RD-2 review is applied segment by segment.
Conceded: the GPS record (F4) is a system record that defeats the driver's statement (F11); the segment 17:37–17:50 adding 3.17 km is not exempt, so the driver fails RD-1 as to that segment.

Conceded as to exemption: the rider named no location (F9) and the driver chose the store (F11), at 5306 m from the pickup (F2), so RD-3(b) denies exemption; the stop duration alone is dealt with under RD-3(c) and is chargeable waiting time.
Conceded: with no incidents near the route (F14) and only band 4 speeds on PIE and CTE (F12, F13), RD-4 gives the driver no justification for the segment, and band 4 is not even a band 1–2 record.

We do not contest this point: the rider's 17:33 message named no store (F9) and the 17:37 segment start (F4) means no location was agreed beforehand, so RD-5 does not exempt the segment — but the pre-departure request itself remains evidence the stop was passenger-initiated.

Agreed on the rate: the bill's distance component of $27.11 over 19.2 km is $1.41/km (F8), which is the rate RD-2 uses; but the $5.30 'excess distance billed' line (F5) is not a separate charge to be refunded on top — it is the distance component already inside that $27.11 and the $41.17 total.

The $4.47 figure (3.17 km × $1.41/km, F4 and F8) is the correct RD-2 measure and is exactly the partial refund the driver's brief offers; no ERP/toll item exists in the bill to add (F8 has no toll line, and FARE-2 is not triggered).
Agreed: the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) matches the $1.08 waiting charge at $0.26/min (F6), which RD-3(c) permits on a metered RydeTAXI trip; the rider withdraws nothing here and we ask no refund of it.

RD-6's flag_account requires the route-dispute upheld count to be ≥ 1 plus this case; the profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 (F17), so the threshold is met only by this single case and the driver's 4.2-year, 4.83-rating, 386-trip record (F17) does not warrant an account review.

You'll get a $4.47 Ryde voucher for the extra distance. The $1.08 waiting charge stays, since that was regular metered wait time. Nothing else changes on your account.
